title: Accept keypad digits on the lock screen while NumLock is desynced
head: 701b87e82da7
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Entering a remapped keypad digit does not replace an existing password selection
leads.consequence: Select the existing password (for example Ctrl+A), then press keypad 1 when its event arrives as KP_End: insert(cursorPosition, '1') appends the digit to the original text rather than replacing the selection. Subsequent typing can authenticate with the wrong password. Qt's public TextInput.insert(position,text) does not remove the selection, unlike its ordinary key insertion path. Clear the selection with remove(selectionStart,selectionEnd) and insert at selectionStart, or use an editing API that replaces selection, while preserving the read-only guard.
leads.triage: corroborated; Same as Opus Q4-B (selection not replaced); published as new finding N1 with Opus harness evidence.

leads.summary: Modified keypad navigation keys are converted to digits instead of moving or selecting
leads.consequence: On the shipped keypad mapping with NumLock off, Shift+keypad End (KP1) is still a navigation keysym but Qt also sets ShiftModifier and KeypadModifier. The handler checks only KeypadModifier, inserts '1', accepts the event and prevents the field's Shift+End selection. Ctrl+keypad Home similarly inserts '7' in place of document navigation. Plain keypad navigation with intentionally disabled NumLock is converted too, since the event has no 'desynced' signal. Restrict the workaround to an independently verified desync condition if preserving navigation is required, and explicitly decide what to do with Shift/Ctrl/Alt combinations rather than catching every KeypadModifier event.
leads.triage: not_material; Behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-modifiers.md): modifier+keypad events all type digits at head; for desynced users an improvement, for deliberate NumLock-off users same trade-off already disclosed in prior review. Not published.

leads.summary: The absolute Qt NumLock desynchronization premise conflicts with the shipped Wayland focus path
leads.consequence: The code comment says Qt never reads the compositor's NumLock state at startup. In Hyprland 0.56.2, setting keyboard focus sends the current locked modifier mask immediately after enter; Qt Wayland 6.11.2 applies that mask with xkb_state_update_mask before translating later keys. Stock Omarchy requests numlock_by_default=true. Therefore the absolute startup premise does not hold on the ordinary lock focus path. This source trace does not prove the reported symptom cannot occur on another path or another version. Reproduce and identify that path before relying on unconditional remapping of deliberate NumLock-off navigation.
leads.triage: corroborated; Same as Opus Q4-C; published as a documentation note, softened to the Qt 6.11.2 source trace and the #8552 discussion.

leads.summary: New test passes even with the entire QML keypad handler disconnected
leads.consequence: The Node test checks only LockModel.keypadDigit and never loads LockView or sends a Qt key event. A sandbox mutant replacing the only call in Keys.onPressed with `else if (false)` passes all fourteen assertions, so the tested head could still have no lock-screen workaround. Add a Qt/Quickshell fixture for at least one desynced KeypadModifier event, a plain navigation key, and the read-only and selection cases, or a structural assertion tied to the handler if a compositor is unavailable.
leads.triage: corroborated_partially; Opus noted the same coverage gap. Sol's mutant run lacked a postcondition that the replacement occurred, so it is not cited; the published claim rests on the test file contents (only loads LockModel.js).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12667#issuecomment-5789260298) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12667#issuecomment-5825032888), checked at `701b87e8`.

**Resolved:** the keypad decimal key no longer types `.` on comma layouts. `701b87e8` removes the `Key_Delete` → `.` mapping and leaves the handler unchanged.

**Verified** with a Qt 6.11.2 test harness that drives the real `LockView.qml` field with synthesized key events:

| Desynced keypad keys: 7, 1, decimal, 4 (arriving as Home, End, Delete, Left) | Field text |
|---|---|
| Base branch | `""` |
| `828ac788` | `71.4` |
| `701b87e8` | `714` |

The reply's "falls through to the field as before" is accurate. While desynced, the decimal key arrives as Delete with no text on both dot and comma layouts, and the field handles it as a forward delete, as on the base branch. With the cursor at the end and nothing selected it changes nothing, so a password containing a keypad decimal still needs NumLock toggled. For example, keypad `12.5` submits `125`.

The earlier verified statements still hold at this head: desynced keypad keys type digits, the number row and dedicated navigation keys pass through, and nothing is inserted while authenticating. The branch merges cleanly with the current `quattro` tip, and `lock-keypad-test.sh` passes on that merge.

### Keypad digits do not replace a selection

This is present since `828ac788`; the new commit did not introduce it. [`LockView.qml:63`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/701b87e82da7a20dddd2d17ea4ae86ead0fd62d9/shell/plugins/lock/LockView.qml#L63) calls `passwordInput.insert(passwordInput.cursorPosition, digit)`. In Qt 6.11.2 the public `TextInput.insert()` keeps an existing selection, while typed text replaces it. Harness results:

| After typing `ab`, then Ctrl+A | Field text |
|---|---|
| Number-row 7, 1 | `71` |
| Desynced keypad 7, 1 | `ab71` |

**Impact:** selecting the password to retype it with keypad digits submits the old text plus the new digits. The attempt fails, and in the masked field the cause is easy to miss.

**Suggested change:** remove the selection before inserting:

```qml
if (passwordInput.selectionStart !== passwordInput.selectionEnd)
  passwordInput.remove(passwordInput.selectionStart, passwordInput.selectionEnd)
```

In the same harness this makes the Ctrl+A case type `71` and leaves the other cases unchanged. #10530 uses the same `insert` pattern in the polkit dialog.

**Optional test improvement:** `lock-keypad-test.sh` loads only `LockModel.js`, so it would still pass if the `Keys.onPressed` branch in `LockView.qml` were removed. The existing Quickshell-driven `lock-password-overflow-test.sh` and its fixture show a way to cover the `KeypadModifier` gate, the read-only guard and the selection case.

**Documentation:** the PR description's test plan still says keypad Home, End and Delete type `71.`; at this head they type `71`, and the decimal key still needs the NumLock toggle. Separately, the comment at `LockModel.js:1-2` attributes the desync to QTBUG-32687, a Qt 5.1 report closed in 2013. In Qt 6.11.2's Wayland client, the compositor's locked modifiers are applied and are lost when a later keymap event creates a fresh keyboard state, which matches the cause discussed recently in #8552. Naming the actual trigger would make it clearer when the workaround can be removed.

**Related open PRs:** #11072 also adds `shell/plugins/lock/LockModel.js` with different helpers; a simulated merge reports an add/add conflict, so whichever lands second has to combine the two files. #10530 still maps keypad Delete to `.`, so the two helpers now disagree on the decimal key if they are folded together as the PR description proposes.

---

**Test scope:** source inspection of the new head, the previously reviewed head and the base, with Qt 6.11.2, libxkbcommon 1.13.2 and xkeyboard-config 2.48. The PR's test was run in an isolated sandbox at the head and on a simulated merge with the current base. A Qt 6.11.2 QML test harness drove `LockView.qml` offscreen with stubbed shell modules and synthesized key events. No live keyboard, compositor, lock surface or PAM authentication was used. The related-PR search was keyword-based, not exhaustive.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
